title: Customer-managed Network Evidence Catalog and SLO Proposal
content:
Goal

Provide a practical, customer-facing PRD draft that defines an "evidence catalog" for customer-managed networking (VPC / on-prem adapters) and ties specific audit log artifacts to approval gates and SLOs. This doc is intentionally scoped to the handoff + ongoing audit surface — how Redwood requests and retains proof, how we sample, and what thresholds/baselines trigger manual review or automated approvals.

Why this matters

- Customers running Redwood Private want a clear, minimal, and automatable set of proof elements we can ask for during onboarding and for periodic attestation.
- Current PRDs focus on policy and change gates but do not enumerate the concrete log fields/events we need for forensicability or the sampling rules for cost/scale.
- Without a lean evidence catalog, approvals become ad-hoc, lengthening time-to-onboard and increasing operational load.

Non-goals

- This doc does NOT attempt to fully define RBAC models or cryptographic key formats (those belong in security and infra PRDs).
- Not prescribing on-prem agent implementation details. We assume the customer has an agent or syslog export endpoint.

High-level proposal summary

1) Evidence catalog: canonical list of event types and minimal schema properties we will request from customer-managed networking components. Think of it as a CSV schema we can ask for via the onboarding checklist or automated connector.
2) Approval gate mapping: map each evidence element to a gate (onboarding: initial approval, maintenance: monthly attestation, emergency changes: immediate review) and to which team reviews it (solutions eng, SRE, security).
3) SLOs & sampling rules: define SLOs for event availability (e.g., 99.9% of expected events present for last 30 days) and sampling heuristics for high-volume customers to limit storage/cost while preserving forensic capability.
4) Templates & playbooks: short approval templates that reviewers can copy into approval tickets with checkboxes and required artifacts.

Evidence catalog (recommended minimal fields)

Note: this is intentionally conservative — start small and expand. Each row below is a deliverable field name and why it matters. We assume UTF-8, newline-delimited JSON or CSV exports are acceptable.

- event_timestamp (required): ISO8601 UTC timestamp for ordering and correlating across sources
- event_id (recommended): stable unique id per event (if available) for dedup and traceability
- source_component (required): short string identifier: eg. customer-firewall, customer-bgp, customer-nat, crossconnect-lb, host-connector
- customer_vpc_id (required): customer-provided VPC id or tenancy identifier to scope events
- change_type (required if event relates to config): enum {CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, DENY, ALLOW, POLICY-APPLY, ROLLBACK}
- actor_identity (strongly_recommended): user@domain or service-account id initiating the change/event
- before_hash / after_hash (optional): for config-change events, short hash of pre/post config payload for compact diffs
- src_ip / dst_ip (for flow events): IPv4/IPv6 strings; allow null for control-plane events
- port / proto (if applicable): numeric port and protocol label
- action (for firewall/NAT): enum {ACCEPT, DROP, REJECT, FORWARD}
- decision_reason (optional): free text short reason from device or policy engine
- related_ticket (optional): link to customer change ticket or Correlation ID provided during handoff
- proof_blob_url (optional): URL/manifest to archived evidence (pcap, config snapshot), ideally time-limited signed URL
- retention_class (optional): suggested retention class label (hot/warm/cold) so Redwood knows expected availability for SLOs

Approval gate mapping examples

- Initial Onboarding Gate (mandatory): require last 7 days of config-change events + firewall policy snapshots + BGP adjacency logs.
  - Required artifacts: event_timestamp, source_component, customer_vpc_id, change_type, actor_identity, proof_blob_url (policy snapshots), related_ticket
  - Reviewer: solutions-eng + security
  - Acceptance criteria: no unexplained admin-originated deny rules; BGP sessions stable for 48 hours; all ingress control plane changes documented in related_ticket.

- Major Network Change Gate (when a change is flagged as major by customer): require pre/post config hashes, actor_identity, and a signed approval artifact.
  - Required artifacts: event_timestamp, event_id, before_hash, after_hash, actor_identity, related_ticket
  - Reviewer: security + SRE
  - Acceptance criteria: approval signature present, rollback plan in related_ticket.

- Continuous Maintenance Attestation (monthly sampling): sample 1 day per week of flow logs + 72 hours of config audit trail.
  - Required artifacts: aggregated flow record (src/dst/port/action), sample index, retention_class
  - Reviewer: automated policy checks with human escalation threshold (>1% unexplained policy drift).

SLOs and sampling rules (practical heuristics)

- Event availability SLO: for required onboarding artifacts, 99.5% of days in last 30 must contain >= 95% of expected event types. Reason: gives slack for one-day outages during handoff.
- Freshness SLO: config-change events must be available within 10 minutes of occurrence for 99% of events during onboarding period. (We can relax to 30m for high-throughput environments.)
- Sampling for flow logs: if raw flow events exceed 20M/day, use deterministic reservoir sampling (hash on src_ip+dst_ip+minute) to retain at most 2M/day for Redwood storage; customer must retain full raw logs for 90 days and provide indices on request.
- Retention tiers: onboarding-critical artifacts (policy snapshots, BGP adjacencies, major change hashes) must be retained hot for 90 days, warm for 365 days. Flow aggregates can be warm/cold as negotiated.

Operational playbook snippets (copy-paste friendly)

- Onboarding ticket template (to attach to customer change):
  - Summary: VPC handoff: <customer_vpc_id>
  - Required artifacts attached: [policy-snapshot-YYYYMMDD], [bgp-adj-YYYYMMDD], [syslog-export-7d]
  - Reviewer checklist:
    - [ ] policy snapshot present and schema-complete
    - [ ] all admin actors in actor_identity are known contacts or service accounts
    - [ ] BGP uptime >= 48h
    - [ ] no anonymous deny entries

- Emergency change review quick-steps:
  - Pull last 2 hours of change_type events for source_component in question
  - Verify before_hash and after_hash; if missing, request immediate snapshot and escalate
  - If actor_identity unknown, pause and request identity confirmation; if critical fix, perform after-action triage and escalate to security

Sample CSV export header (compact example)

"event_timestamp,event_id,source_component,customer_vpc_id,change_type,actor_identity,before_hash,after_hash,src_ip,dst_ip,port,proto,action,decision_reason,related_ticket,proof_blob_url,retention_class"

Implementation notes and integration paths

- Preferred ingestion methods: s3-compatible signed object drop, syslog-collector endpoint, or a small agent that can push batched NDJSON to a collector. We should support 3 modes for onboarding to reduce friction.
- Validation: a lightweight schema validator we ship as part of solutions-eng tooling (python script + quick CLI) to check required fields and run simple sanity checks (timestamp monotonicity, hash lengths, enumerations).
- Automation: wire up automated pre-checks that run on ticket creation and mark the ticket ready/blocked. The pre-check should compute evidence coverage scores and attach the score to the ticket.

Open questions (for engineering/security/product)

1) What is the canonical identity format we demand for actor_identity? email/service-account/opaque uuid? Need consensus for cross-correlation across customers.
2) For proofs (pcap/config snapshots), do we accept only signed URLs or prefer customer-supplied manifest + signature? Legal may prefer signed manifests.
3) Sampling algorithm: deterministic reservoir sampling proposal above — does infra prefer a different approach to make replays deterministic across regions?
4) How do we surface SLO violation reasons to customers without leaking internal reviewer comments? Need templated language.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: asking for too many artifacts kills adoption. Mitigation: break checklist into "must-have" and "nice-to-have" and only require must-have for initial approval. Use optional artifacts for deeper audits.
- Risk: storage/cost blowup from raw flows. Mitigation: aggressive sampling + require long-term retention on customer side. Provide compression/aggregation tooling.
- Risk: customer unwilling to provide actor_identity in cleartext. Mitigation: allow hashed identities with an agreed salt for correlation during onboarding (but require a way for customer to reveal identity in escalations).

Next steps (short-term roadmap)

- Dec 2025: finalize minimal evidence catalog and schema; create lightweight validator script (solutions-eng + applied-ml to help create heuristics)
- Jan 2026: pilot with 2 customers (one cloud-hosted VPC, one on-prem) and iterate sampling rules
- Feb 2026: bake automated pre-check into our onboarding workflow and create reviewer checklist templates in Console

Notes to reviewers

This is intentionally pragmatic and lightweight. Focus review on (1) are the required fields minimal and sufficient for forensicability, (2) are the SLOs reasonable and defensible to customers, (3) are the sampling heuristics operationally implementable.
